sections.label: The opening
sections.line: The experiment of running a sovereign website, and everything that makes it, on one Raspberry Pi at home.

sections.label: In short
sections.line: A Pi 5 with 16GB and 256GB; six parts; what we measure; nothing leaves the house; a product after the Kickstarter.

sections.label: Why a Pi
sections.line: A site on a computer the owner holds, made by a model the owner runs, under rules the owner can read.

sections.label: The six parts
sections.line: Serve from home, take only signed updates, run a local model, build a site on the Pi, back up to a vault, reach it from outside.

sections.label: What we will measure
sections.line: Model speed, time per site, quality against cloud models, power, and what breaks; all published with the recipe.

sections.label: What could go wrong
sections.line: Slow models, smaller than hoped, a slow card; the honest result may be a split with cloud models.

sections.label: From experiment to product
sections.line: The prototype for the Raspberry Pi sovereign website, launching officially once the Kickstarter finishes.

sections.label: What this does not claim
sections.line: Nothing run yet; tools are candidates; no speed or quality claims until measured.

sections.label: Where this comes from
sections.line: The launch plan, the build page, the sovereign website principles and how a vault works.
